content.user_title: Build Reliable TanStack Data and Routing
content.value_statement: Duplicated server state and inconsistent query keys can cause stale data and unnecessary requests. This skill guides TanStack patterns for caching, mutations, routing, and rendering.
actual_capabilities: Guide structured query keys, reusable query options, cancellation signals, and intentional cache freshness.
Explain mutation invalidation and optimistic updates with snapshots, rollback, and concurrency caveats.
Guide typed routing, validated search parameters, and loader integration with the Query cache.
Explain server prefetching and client hydration for TanStack Start applications.
Provide guidance on stable table inputs, form state validation, and accessible virtualization.
Distinguish shared server data, URL state, and local UI state without requiring a stack migration.
limitations: Provides written guidance and illustrative snippets, not executable tooling or automated verification.
Assumes an existing or explicitly selected TanStack project; it does not require adopting the entire stack.
The optimistic mutation example assumes serialized writes and a fixed query key; concurrent writes need additional reconciliation.
Examples rely on application-specific fetchers and update helpers; Table, Form, Virtual, and Start coverage is brief.

use_cases.title: Improve Query Cache Consistency
use_cases.description: Review query keys, freshness settings, and mutation invalidation in an existing React application.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Routes and Server Data
use_cases.description: Plan validated URL filters, loader prefetching, and shared Query hydration for a TanStack Router or Start project.

use_cases.title: Review Data-Heavy Interfaces
use_cases.description: Assess stable table inputs, form drafts, and measured virtualization needs while preserving accessible navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Server and UI State
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component in our existing TanStack Query project. Identify server data, URL state, and local UI state. Explain which duplicated state needs removal.

prompt_templates.title: Define Reusable Query Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our filtered list query. Propose reusable query options with complete keys, cancellation signals, and an appropriate staleTime. Preserve the existing data API.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve caching and query reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Connect URL Filters and Loaders
prompt_templates.prompt: In our TanStack Router project, design validated search parameters for filters and pagination. Integrate loaders with Query using ensureQueryData without duplicating URL state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: coordinate navigation and data loading.

prompt_templates.title: Review Concurrent Optimistic Mutations
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit our optimistic list updates for concurrent writes and changing filters. Explain rollback risks and propose reconciliation that preserves newer updates and query identity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess mutation correctness under concurrency.

output_examples.input: Our filtered list shows stale results after saving. What should we review?
output: Include every data-changing filter in the query key.
Reuse the same query options in components and loaders.
Invalidate affected queries after mutations so the cache reconciles with server data.
Check staleTime against the expected freshness of this list.

output_examples.input: Should a sortable table put filters in component state or the URL?
output: Use validated Router search parameters for shareable filters and pagination.
Keep temporary editing drafts and purely local interactions in component state.
Keep Table columns stable and provide data with the stability required by the table integration.
Add virtualization only when measured rendering costs justify it.

output_examples.input: Can we use the snapshot rollback example for overlapping optimistic edits?
output: The example assumes serialized mutations and a fixed list key.
Restoring an older snapshot can erase a newer optimistic update.
Use mutation-aware reconciliation or derive optimistic UI from pending mutation variables.
Ensure optimistic changes respect the list filter and reconcile with server data.

best_practices: Use only the TanStack libraries selected by the project and preserve justified framework loaders or external integrations.
Include all data dependencies in query keys and reuse query options across components and loaders.
Test rollback, concurrent writes, filter changes, and accessible navigation when applying the relevant guidance.
anti_patterns: Introduce the entire TanStack stack for generic React work without an explicit project decision.
Maintain redundant copies of shared server data or URL filters in component state.
Apply snapshot rollback to overlapping mutations without accounting for newer updates.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does this skill install TanStack packages?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed file provides written guidance and examples, not installation commands or package automation.

faq.question: Must my project use every TanStack library?
faq.answer: No. Apply only the libraries already selected by the project. A working framework loader does not require migration.

faq.question: Does the skill include complete application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides illustrative Query snippets and broader library guidance. Fetchers, mutation handlers, and optimistic-update helpers remain application-specific.

faq.question: Is the optimistic update example safe for concurrent writes?
faq.answer: Not without adaptation. The example assumes serialized mutations and a fixed key. Concurrent writes need mutation-aware reconciliation or pending-variable optimistic UI.

faq.question: What did the security review find?
faq.answer: All 25 static alerts were false positives. No evidence found of command execution, keylogging, reconnaissance, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md.
